title: Flight Control Intern - Stabilizing Unstable Aircraft
description: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. About the role As a Flight Control Intern, you explore how far an aircraft can be pushed beyond natural stability, and what performance that buys. Instability makes aircraft more agile, but only if the control system can keep them flying. You own your project end to end: you choose and build unstable airframes, identify their dynamics from flight data, design the control that stabilizes them, and measure the limits of what can be achieved. You work on agile, high-performance platforms in a fast-paced engineering team with an industrial, production-first mindset, flying frequently on a dedicated test range. You are a full member of the team, with visibility on how the company and its products evolve and a direct impact on what we ship. Responsibilities Select and justify unstable configurations to study, such as multirotor and VTOL (vertical take-off and landing), relaxed-stability fixed wings, and tailless, blended-wing or canard layouts. Design and build the airframes yourself (foam, 3D printing, composites), integrate the avionics provided by the team, and repair after crashes. Plan and run flight test campaigns with excitation maneuvers, and iterate quickly on a dedicated test range. Identify the aircraft dynamics from flight data (system identification) and validate the models against analytical and simulated results. Design and tune stabilizing controllers on PX4 or ArduPilot, then port them to Harmattan's in-house flight controller firmware. Push the instability step by step, for example by moving the center of gravity aft or reducing control surfaces, and analyze stability margins. Quantify the performance envelope, including the limits set by actuator bandwidth, sensor noise and latency, and the agility gained in return. Build a reusable toolchain: a Python simulation workflow (for example JSBSim or Gazebo) validated on flight data, hardware-in-the-loop tests, flight test procedures and a data analysis pipeline. Present concepts, results, and project status to the team and to wider audiences, and join team meetings to learn from other projects. Candidate Requirements Currently pursuing an MSc in Aerospace Engineering, Control, Robotics, or a related field. Solid foundations in flight mechanics and control theory, ideally with experience in system identification or stability analysis. Proficiency in Python. C/C++ and embedded firmware experience is a plus. Hands-on building experience, such as RC aircraft, drones, or any fabrication project. Familiarity with PX4 or ArduPilot is a plus. Comfort with flight testing, debugging in the field, and learning from the occasional crash. Motivated, autonomous, and proactive, with the ability to own a project and communicate results clearly.
